οὐ πολὺς ἦν ἄγαν παρ' αὐτοῖς ὁ λόγος. Ταύτῃ τοι πρὸς αὐτοὺς καὶ αὐτὸς ἔφασκεν ὁ
Σωτήρ· "6Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, Γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταὶ, ὅτι ἀποδεκατοῦτε τὸ
ἄνηθον καὶ τὸ ἡδύοσμον, καὶ τὸ κύμινον. Καὶ ἀφήκατε τὰ βαρύτερα τοῦ νόμου, τὴν
κρίσιν, καὶ τὸ ἔλεος, καὶ τὴν πίστιν."6 Ἦσαν οὖν ἄρα φιλοκερδεῖς καὶ ἐρασι-
χρήματοι, καὶ πικρὰς ἔσθ' ὅτε τοῖς πταίουσιν ἐπῆγον τὰς δίκας, ἵνα ἐκδειματοῦντες
τοὺς ἐφ' ὁτῳοῦν ἐγκα- λουμένους προσάγειν αὐτοῖς ἀναπείθωσιν καὶ τὰ ὑπὲρ
δύναμιν ἔσθ' ὅτε. Ταύτῃ τοί φησι πρὸς τοὺς παρ' αὐτῶν ἀδικουμένους· "6Λαός μου,
οἱ πράκτορες ὑμῶν καλαμῶνται ὑμᾶς, καὶ οἱ ἀπαιτοῦντες κυριεύουσιν ὑμῶν."6 Καὶ
διὰ μὲν τοῦ λαὸν εἰπεῖν, ἔτι τὸν Ἰσραὴλ δίδωσι νοεῖν, ὡς εἴπερ ἕλοιντο μεταφοιτᾷν
ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτῷ δοκοῦν, τῶν ἐξ ἡμερότητος τεύξονται καὶ φιλ- ανθρωπίας, καὶ οὐκ
εἰσάπαν ἀποπεσοῦνται τῆς πρὸς αὐτὸν οἰκειότητος σχετικῆς. Καλαμᾶσθαι δὲ εἰπὼν
τοὺς πράκτορας, τῆς ἐνούσης αὐτοῖς ἀπλη- στίας τε ὁμοῦ καὶ φιλοκερδίας δείκνυσι
τὸ μέγεθος. Ἐν μὲν γὰρ τοῖς ληΐοις οἱ μὲν ἀποκείρουσι σιδήρῳ τὸν στάχυν, οἱ δὲ
τοὺς ἐκπίπτοντας τῆς τοῦ κείροντος χειρὸς συλλέγοντες, οὐδὲν ἀφιᾶσιν ἐν ἀγροῖς.
Ἔθος δὲ καὶ τοῖς τὰς ἀμπέλους τρυγῶσι τοῦτο δρᾷν. "6Κα- λαμῶνται τοίνυν ὑμᾶς,
φησὶν, οἱ πράκτορες ὑμῶν."6 Ὅμοιον ὡς εἰ λέγοι· Τετρυγήκασιν ὑμῶν τὰς πε-
ριουσίας, καὶ οὐ μέχρι τούτου τὰ τῆς ἀπληστίας αὐτοῖς. Ἀλλ' ἤδη καὶ καλαμῶνται, 38 τοῦτ' ἔστι, τὰς χεῖρας ἐπάγουσι, καὶ τοῖς ἔτι καταλελειμμένοις. Εὖ δὲ δὴ σφόδρα, καὶ
πρεπόντως αὐτοῖς, οὐ καθηγητὰς, οὐ διδασκάλους, οὐχ ἕτερόν τι τῶν τοιούτων
εἶναί φησιν, πράκτορας δὲ ὀνομάζει, καὶ ἀπαιτητάς. ∆ι- δάσκει δὲ ὅτι
κατεξουσιάζουσιν αὐτῶν, οὐχ ὡς δι- δάσκαλοι μαθηταῖς ἠπίως προσφερόμενοι, ἀλλ'
οἷον σκληροὶ καὶ ἄγριοι δεσπόται, τὸ δοκοῦν αὐτοῖς φρονεῖν ἀναγκάζοντες, καὶ
πρὸς πᾶν ὁτιοῦν ἀποφέ- ροντες, καὶ τῶν παρὰ γνώμην ἔσθ' ὅτε. Ἀλλ' ὅ γε τῶν ἐν
Χριστῷ σκοπὸς οὐ τοιοῦτος ἦν. Γράφει γοῦν ὁ θεσπέσιος Πέτρος τοῖς κεκλημένοις
εἰς ἐπισκοπὴν, καὶ καθηγεῖσθαι λαχοῦσι τῶν λογικῶν ποιμνίων, μὴ ὡς
κατακυριεύοντες τῶν κλήρων, ἀλλὰ τύποι γενόμε- νοι τοῦ ποιμνίου. Οἶδεν δὲ ὁ
λόγος ὁ μυστικὸς καὶ πράκτορας ἑτέρους, οὓς ἀνάγκη παραιτεῖσθαι τοῖς ἐθέλουσι
βιοῦν ὀρθῶς. Αἱ γὰρ πονηραὶ καὶ ἀντι- κείμεναι δυνάμεις ἕκαστον τῶν ἐπὶ γῆς
μονονουχὶ καὶ ἀπαιτοῦσι τὴν εἰς τὸ φαῦλον σπουδὴν, καὶ ὥσπερ τινὰ δασμὸν παρ'
ἡμῶν συλλέγουσι, τὴν εἰς τὰ πάθη τῆς διανοίας ῥοπήν. Καὶ γοῦν ὁ ἱερὸς μακαρίζει
pass_a_gloss: [...] was giving. And the aim was to them, and it had been set with all zeal, to persuade those [people] of the need to keep the law in these things most of all; but of the other commandments there was not very much account among them. For this reason the Saviour himself also was saying to them: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you tithe the dill and the mint and the cumin. And you left the weightier things of the law, the judgment and the mercy and the faith. So they were lovers of gain and lovers of money, and sometimes they were bringing bitter penalties on those who stumbled, so that, terrifying those charged with anything whatever, they might persuade them to bring to them even the things beyond power sometimes. For this reason he says to those wronged by them: My people, your exactors glean you, and those who demand rule over you. And through saying people, he gives Israel still to understand that, if they should choose to move over to what seems good to him, they will obtain the things from gentleness and loving-kindness, and will not wholly fall away from the close kinship toward him. And having said that the exactors glean, he shows the greatness of the insatiability and love of gain being in them together. For in the cornfields some cut off the ear with iron, and others, gathering the [ears] falling from the hand of the one cutting, leave nothing in fields. And it is custom also for those gathering the grapes of the vines to do this. They glean then you, he says, your exactors. Similar as if he should say: They have harvested your possessions, and the things of the insatiability are not to them as far as this. But already they also glean, that is, they bring their hands upon those things still left. And very well indeed, and fittingly to them, he says they are not guides, not teachers, nor any other of such things, but names them exactors and demanders. And he teaches that they lord it over them, not as teachers bearing themselves gently toward disciples, but as harsh and savage masters, forcing [them] to think what seems good to them, and carrying them toward anything whatever, even of the things against judgment sometimes. But the aim of those in Christ was not such. So the divine Peter writes to those called into oversight, and whose lot is to lead the rational flocks, not as lording it over the lots, but becoming types of the flock. And the mystical account knows also other exactors, whom those wishing to live rightly must refuse. For the wicked and opposing powers all but demand of each of those on earth the zeal toward the base, and as some tribute collect from us the leaning of the mind toward the passions. And indeed the holy [one] calls blessed [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: Their aim, pursued with all their zeal, was to persuade people that the law had to be kept in these matters above all; of the other commandments they took little account. That is why the Savior himself said to them: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you tithe dill and mint and cumin, and have neglected the weightier matters of the law: justice and mercy and faith” (Matthew 23:23).

So they were greedy for gain and lovers of money. At times they brought harsh penalties on those who slipped, so that by terrifying anyone accused of anything at all they might induce them to bring offerings, sometimes even beyond their means. That is why he says to those they wronged: “My people, your exactors glean you, and those who demand payment rule over you” (Isaiah 3:12).

By saying “people” he still gives Israel to understand that if they chose to turn to what pleases him, they would meet with his gentleness and love for humankind, and would not fall away altogether from their close bond with him.

By saying that the exactors glean, he shows how great their insatiable greed for gain was. In the cornfields some cut the ears with iron, while others gather the stalks that fall from the reaper’s hand and leave nothing in the fields. Those who harvest vines usually do the same. “So your exactors glean you,” he says. It is as if he said: They have harvested your wealth, and their greed does not stop there. They are already gleaning as well, that is, laying their hands even on what is still left.

Very well and fittingly he does not call them guides or teachers or anything of the kind; he names them exactors and collectors. He teaches that they lord it over the people, not dealing gently with them as teachers with disciples, but like harsh and savage masters, forcing them to think as they see fit and driving them to anything at all, at times even against their own judgment.

But the aim of those in Christ was not of this kind. The inspired Peter writes to those called to oversight, whose lot it is to lead the rational flocks: “not as lording it over those in your charge, but being examples to the flock” (1 Peter 5:3).

The mystical sense also knows of other exactors, whom those who wish to live rightly must refuse. For the wicked and hostile powers all but demand of everyone on earth eagerness for what is base, and collect from us a kind of tribute: the mind’s leaning toward the passions. And indeed the holy … calls blessed …

choices.why: The clause had been missing and is restored: the accused were pressed to give beyond their power.
The image of gleaners after the reapers shows the collectors' insatiable greed.
rejected: use the metaphor of threshing floors

choices.english: he names them exactors and collectors
choices.why: Cyril notes that the prophet withholds the name of teachers.
1 Peter 5:3, set against leaders who lord it over the people.
